DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
The random trial in this paper is well designed, and the price arithmetic is correct. But the paper misreports its own results. **ParcelLine failed two of the three measurable requirements** in the trial. Once the paper's own £48 cost of damage and loss is included, ParcelLine becomes the **most expensive** carrier, not the cheapest. The customer-contact advantage is also confounded by a text-message test that only ParcelLine's parcels received. On the trial evidence, **SwiftDrop** is the cheapest carrier that complies with the requirements.

## 1. ParcelLine failed the service requirements

Section 2 sets the requirements: **on-time delivery of at least 95%** and **damage below 0.5%**. Table 1 shows:

| Carrier | On-time (requirement ≥95%) | Damage (requirement <0.5%) |
|---|---|---|
| SwiftDrop | 96.2% ✓ | 0.4% ✓ |
| ParcelLine | **93.1% ✗** | **0.9% ✗** |
| Meridian | 97.5% ✓ | 0.3% ✓ |

The statement in section 3, "on-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers", is wrong, and so is the recommendation's claim that ParcelLine "met our service requirements". ParcelLine also loses parcels at about three to four times the rate of the others.

With about 5,000 parcels per carrier, these differences are larger than chance would explain. For example, 0.9% damage is about 45 damaged parcels, compared with about 20 for SwiftDrop.

## 2. Including damage and loss reverses the ranking

Section 2 says each damaged or lost parcel costs **£48**. The cost comparison leaves this out. At 42,000 parcels a month:

| Carrier | Delivery cost | Damaged and lost parcels | Cost of damage and loss | WISMO contacts at £3.20 | **Total per month** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SwiftDrop | £149,100 | 168 + 13 ≈ 181 | £8,670 | £1,478 | **£159,250** |
| ParcelLine | £146,160 | 378 + 34 ≈ 412 | £19,760 | £806 | **£166,720** |
| Meridian | £152,460 | 126 + 8 ≈ 134 | £6,450 | £1,344 | **£160,250** |

On this basis:
- ParcelLine is about **£7,500 a month (around £90,000 a year) more expensive** than SwiftDrop.
- It is about **£6,500 a month (around £78,000 a year)** more expensive than Meridian.
- These figures **include** ParcelLine's customer-contact saving.

The claimed £35,000–£76,000 annual saving is in fact a loss of roughly that size. These totals also leave out the cost of late deliveries and the extra one-star reviews that section 2 links to damage.

## 3. The customer-contact advantage is confounded

Section 5 says that "from 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message". That covers half of the trial, and **only ParcelLine's** parcels received it. Fewer "where is my order?" contacts is exactly what a proactive delivery text would be expected to produce. The claim that ParcelLine's app "clearly reduces customer contacts" is therefore unsupported.

ParcelLine also had the **most late deliveries**, which would normally *increase* "where is my order?" contacts. That makes the text message the more likely explanation. Since the text is being rolled out to all carriers anyway, the advantage will probably disappear.

## 4. Peak-season risk

- The trial ran in April and May, which is off-peak.
- The contract starts on 1 October, just before peak season.
- ParcelLine's references are "mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels", while SwiftDrop and Meridian have handled similar peak volumes.

The heavier parcels (lamps, mirrors and small furniture, 30% of volume) are also where damage is most likely. ParcelLine is the weakest of the three on this risk, and the paper doesn't discuss it.

## 5. What holds up

- The trial design is good. Random allocation across about 5,000 parcels per carrier gives a fair comparison.
- The blended prices are correct: £3.55, £3.48 and £3.63.
- The monthly costs and the price differences (£2,940 and £6,300 a month) are correct.
- The contact-cost arithmetic is correct: (11 − 6) × 42 × £3.20 ≈ £672.

## 6. What the evidence actually supports

- **SwiftDrop:** the lowest total cost, meets every requirement, has peak-season experience, and offers a 12-month term.
- **Meridian:** the best service on every measure, and only about £1,000 a month more expensive in total. Against that, it requires a 24-month commitment.
- **ParcelLine:** the lowest price before other costs, but it fails both service thresholds and is the most expensive overall.

## Suggested revisions

1. **Correct the statements about requirements** in sections 3 and 7. ParcelLine missed both the on-time and the damage thresholds.
2. **Add the costs of damage and loss** to the cost comparison, using the paper's own £48 figure, and compare total cost.
3. **Remove the claim about ParcelLine's app**, or rerun the contact comparison with the text message on all carriers or on none.
4. **Address peak-season capability** before a contract starting in October.
5. **Reconsider the recommendation.** On this evidence, SwiftDrop for 12 months is the strongest choice, with Meridian as the higher-service alternative if a 24-month term is acceptable.

As written, the paper would have the company choose the carrier that failed its own service tests and costs the most overall.
